An electronic control unit is equipped with first-system and second-system inverter circuits that drive a multiphase motor separately for each coil set. It also includes first and second phase-voltage detection circuits that sense the voltage of at least one phase in the current supply paths extending from the inverter circuits to the coil sets, and a diagnostic device that identifies faults using the voltages detected by those detection circuits.

When the first-system inverter circuit switches on either the upper-arm or lower-arm switching element for one phase of the first coil set while switching off the other element, and the second-system inverter circuit is placed in a high-impedance output state, the diagnostic device checks the voltage detected by the second phase-voltage detection circuit. If that detected voltage matches the output voltage of the first-system inverter circuit, the diagnostic device concludes that a short-circuit fault has occurred.

An electronic control unit is configured to drive a multiphase motor using a plurality of inverter systems. Specifically, the electronic control unit includes a first inverter system and a second inverter system, each of which supplies drive current to the motor on a coil set basis. Each inverter system includes inverter circuits having switching elements that control the supply of current to the corresponding coil sets of the multiphase motor.

The electronic control unit further includes phase potential detecting circuits. These circuits are provided in current supply paths extending from the inverter circuits to the respective coil sets. A first phase potential detecting circuit detects the phase potentials in the current supply paths associated with the first inverter system, while a second phase potential detecting circuit detects the phase potentials in the current supply paths associated with the second inverter system.

A diagnosis apparatus is provided to detect failures in the electronic control unit based on the potentials measured by the first and second phase potential detecting circuits. By monitoring these detected potentials, the diagnosis apparatus can determine whether an abnormal electrical condition exists between the inverter systems or in the current supply paths.

During a failure diagnosis operation, the first inverter system is controlled so that, for a selected phase, one switching element is turned ON and the other switching element is turned OFF. As a result, the output potential of the first inverter system for that phase is set to a predetermined potential corresponding to the ON state of the selected switching element. At the same time, the second inverter system is controlled to enter a high-impedance output state, in which its switching elements are turned OFF so that the second inverter system does not actively drive the corresponding phase.

While the second inverter system is in the high-impedance state, the diagnosis apparatus compares the potential detected by the second phase potential detecting circuit with the output potential generated by the first inverter system. If the potential detected in the second inverter system corresponds to the output potential of the first inverter system, the diagnosis apparatus determines that a short-circuit failure has occurred between the first inverter system and the second inverter system, or between their associated current supply paths. In this manner, the electronic control unit can accurately diagnose a short-circuit failure by observing whether the output potential of one inverter system appears in the other inverter system while the latter is electrically inactive.
outputs.L4:
An electronic control unit is configured to diagnose short-circuit failures in a drive apparatus that includes a multiphase motor and two inverter systems connected to separate coil sets of the motor. The motor may include a first winding group and a second winding group, each having a plurality of phase coils, and the two inverter systems may independently supply current to the respective winding groups. Because the winding groups are magnetically coupled through the motor, an abnormal electrical connection or short circuit between the two systems can cause a potential generated in one system to appear on a current path of the other system. The electronic control unit detects this abnormal condition by monitoring phase potentials under a predetermined diagnostic state.

During the diagnosis, the electronic control unit controls the switching elements of at least one inverter so that a known inverter output potential is produced in a first system. At the same time, the current path of a corresponding phase in a second system is placed in a high-impedance state, or in another controlled state in which the phase potential can be accurately observed without being actively driven. A voltage detection circuit detects the phase potential on the current path connected to the second coil set. The electronic control unit then compares the detected phase potential of the second system with the inverter output potential of the first system.

If the second system is electrically isolated from the first system, the detected phase potential in the second system should not substantially coincide with the output potential generated by the first system. However, if a short circuit exists between the first and second systems, the output potential of the first inverter system is transmitted to the corresponding current path of the second inverter system. In that case, the detected phase potential of the second system becomes equal to, or falls within a predetermined allowable range of, the inverter output potential of the first system. When this correspondence is detected, the electronic control unit determines that a short-circuit failure has occurred between the systems.

The diagnostic operation may be performed for each phase of the multiphase motor, and the determination may be made by comparing the detected phase potential with one or more reference potentials associated with the switching state of the first inverter. For example, when the first inverter connects a phase to a high-potential-side power line or a low-potential-side power line, the electronic control unit can determine whether the detected potential in the second system follows that high-side or low-side potential. If the detected potential follows the output state of the first system despite the second system being placed in a non-driving or high-impedance condition, the apparatus identifies the presence of an unintended conductive path.

By performing the diagnosis under a controlled switching condition and by using the high-impedance state to prevent the second system from masking the abnormal potential, the apparatus can reliably detect short-circuit failures between the dual inverter systems. This enables early identification of insulation faults, wiring faults, semiconductor failures, or other abnormal connections between the separate coil sets or inverter output paths. As a result, the electronic control unit can take appropriate protective action, such as stopping motor drive, disabling one or both inverter systems, limiting output torque, or notifying a higher-level controller of the failure. The apparatus therefore improves the reliability and safety of a multiphase motor drive system having dual inverter systems.

**Under and Off**

Sometimes life feels like it is happening **under** a heavy cloud, where everything seems quiet, hidden, or uncertain. We may feel under pressure, under stress, or under the weight of responsibilities. In those moments, it is important to pause and remember that difficult times do not last forever.

Turning **off** distractions can help us find clarity. Switching off the noise of phones, worries, and negative thoughts gives the mind space to rest. When we step away from what overwhelms us, we can better understand what we need and where we want to go.

Being under pressure does not mean we are powerless. It can be a sign that we need to slow down, switch off for a while, and take care of ourselves. Sometimes the best way to move forward is to turn off the noise and look under the surface, where real strength often begins.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize this patent claim in one concise paragraph: an ECU with two inverter systems for a multiphase motor, phase potential detection circuits, and a diagnostic device that detects a short circuit when the inactive system’s detected phase potential matches the active system’s output potential.
counterfactuals.output: The claim describes an electronic control unit for a multiphase motor that includes two inverter systems, each connected to corresponding motor windings, along with circuits that detect phase potentials in each system. During operation of one inverter system while the other is inactive, a diagnostic device compares the detected phase potential of the inactive system with the output potential of the active system, and determines that a short circuit exists when those potentials match.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for an electronic control unit that diagnoses short-circuit failure between two motor drive systems using phase potential detecting circuits while one inverter is driven and the other is placed in high impedance.
counterfactuals.output: An electronic control unit for a motor drive apparatus including first and second motor drive systems respectively having first and second inverters is configured to diagnose a short-circuit failure between the motor drive systems. The electronic control unit includes phase potential detecting circuits configured to detect phase potentials of motor lines in at least one of the motor drive systems, and a control circuit configured to execute a failure diagnosis mode in which one of the first and second inverters is driven while the other inverter is placed in a high-impedance state. During the failure diagnosis mode, the control circuit determines whether a short-circuit failure exists between corresponding or non-corresponding phase lines of the first and second motor drive systems based on phase potentials detected by the phase potential detecting circuits in the motor drive system having the inverter placed in the high-impedance state. Accordingly, an inter-system short-circuit failure can be detected without simultaneously energizing both motor drive systems, thereby improving diagnostic reliability and reducing risk of abnormal current flow.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a technical description of a failure diagnosis apparatus for a dual-system inverter ECU, where one system applies an upper or lower arm switching element to a phase and the other system is high impedance, and a short-circuit is detected from corresponding phase potentials.
counterfactuals.output:
A failure diagnosis apparatus is provided for a dual-system inverter ECU having first and second inverter systems connected to a common multi-phase electric load, such as a three-phase motor. Each inverter system includes, for each phase, an upper-arm switching element connected to a high-potential power line and a lower-arm switching element connected to a low-potential power line. The apparatus diagnoses an inter-system or phase-related short-circuit failure by selectively driving one inverter system while placing the other inverter system in a high-impedance state.

The failure diagnosis apparatus includes a control unit configured to execute a diagnostic mode in which, for a selected phase, one of the inverter systems is set as an active-side system and the other inverter system is set as a detection-side system. In the active-side system, either the upper-arm switching element or the lower-arm switching element corresponding to the selected phase is turned on so that the selected phase is driven toward a known reference potential, such as a power-supply potential or a ground potential. The remaining switching elements of the active-side system may be turned off or controlled so as not to interfere with the diagnostic potential.

In the detection-side system, the upper-arm and lower-arm switching elements corresponding to the same phase are both turned off, thereby placing the phase terminal of the detection-side system in a high-impedance condition. A phase-potential detection circuit detects the potential appearing at the corresponding phase terminal of the detection-side system while the selected phase of the active-side system is being forced to the known potential.

When the detected phase potential of the high-impedance detection-side system follows, approaches, or otherwise corresponds to the potential applied by the active-side system, the control unit determines that an abnormal conductive path exists between the corresponding phase terminals or between associated wiring portions of the two inverter systems. For example, if the active-side upper-arm switching element is turned on and the detection-side phase potential rises toward the high-potential power line, or if the active-side lower-arm switching element is turned on and the detection-side phase potential falls toward the low-potential power line, the apparatus determines that a short-circuit failure is present. Conversely, when the detected phase potential remains within an expected floating or non-corresponding range, the control unit determines that no short-circuit is detected for that diagnostic condition.

The diagnosis may be performed sequentially for each phase and for both polarities by applying the upper-arm and lower-arm switching elements in turn. The roles of the first and second inverter systems may also be interchanged so that each system is alternately used as the active-side system and the detection-side system. Based on the combination of the applied switching state and the detected phase potential, the apparatus identifies the phase in which the short-circuit has occurred and may further distinguish whether the abnormality is associated with a high-potential-side short, a low-potential-side short, or an inter-system phase short.

The apparatus may include threshold determination logic for comparing the detected phase potential with predetermined upper and lower determination thresholds. A short-circuit determination is made when the detected potential in the high-impedance system exceeds the upper threshold during upper-arm application by the active system, or falls below the lower threshold during lower-arm application by the active system. The thresholds may be set with margins accounting for leakage current, parasitic capacitance, sensor offset, and transient settling characteristics.

By diagnosing a short-circuit while one inverter system actively applies a known phase potential and the other inverter system is electrically isolated in a high-impedance state, the apparatus can detect abnormal conduction between corresponding phase circuits without requiring normal motor drive operation. This enables reliable failure detection in a dual-system inverter ECU and supports protective actions such as inhibiting inverter operation, isolating the failed system, or notifying a higher-level controller of the diagnosed failure.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a concise claim-like explanation for a motor control ECU that detects shorts between first and second current supply paths using detected phase potentials from two inverter systems driving multiphase motor coil sets.
counterfactuals.output: A motor control ECU includes first and second inverter systems that supply current through respective first and second current supply paths to corresponding multiphase motor coil sets. The ECU detects phase potentials of the respective inverter systems and determines, based on a comparison or correlation of the detected phase potentials, whether an abnormal short circuit exists between the first and second current supply paths. When the phase potentials indicate unintended electrical coupling between the paths, the ECU identifies a short-between-systems fault and performs fault handling for the motor drive.
